followup_explanation:
This query is a well-specified explanatory request: the user wants a structured breakdown of a defined econ concept (price elasticity of demand) and its concrete applications in a specific industry. It has clear scope and completion criteria, which aligns with both models' capabilities well.

I leaned toward Willet for a couple of reasons:

- Its public benchmarks edge slightly higher on knowledge/reasoning (MMLU-Pro 75.9, GPQA 56.2, Arena-Hard 83.2), which is marginally relevant for accurate conceptual explanation.
- While Willet self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, this task isn't truly open-ended — it has a clear topic and bounded scope (pricing, promotions, menu choices). And critically, that self-reported preference is documented as *dissociated from measured capability*, so it doesn't predict lower output quality.

Honestly, the two models are close to a tie here — the internal eval differences on the relevant categories are within variance. So this was a marginal call rather than a strong one. Both would handle it well.
